title: e2e job: align, call, annotate and report on the fixture
description:
Add scripts/ci/e2e-run.sh, which runs every case file `tests/e2e/*.sh` in name order with shared helpers in `tests/e2e/lib.sh`, runs all of them even when one fails, prints a table case / result / log path to the job summary and exits non-zero if any failed (so the red-first run lists every broken step, not only the first). Later packages add their own `tests/e2e/<package-key>-*.sh` and never edit the runner or the workflow. Add job `e2e` in .github/workflows/e2e.yml (ubuntu-latest, 4 vCPU, 16 GB; free disk first by removing the preinstalled Android/.NET/Haskell toolchains). Using the fixture and the mini reference as GENOME_DIR: run setup-less steps 02 (FASTQ to BAM), 03 (DeepVariant, 2.1 GB image), 06, 07 (PharmCAT), 11, 12, 16, 16b, 20, 21, 27, 32 (pypgx with its bundle, 370 MB), 24 and generate-report; steps 30, 23 and 31 on the VEP-annotated subset with one tiny score file; the step-21 and step-12 cases that package fresh-run-works names. A second leg runs `nextflow run main.nf -profile docker` (real containers, today's VCF+BAM samplesheet built from the bash leg's outputs, `--max_cpus 4 --max_memory 14.GB`) with tools clinvar, mosdepth, delly, vcfanno (the same tiny score file), roh, pharmcat and cpic. A last case lists every external http(s) `src`/`href` in the generated HTML reports (pipeline report, PharmCAT, MultiQC) so remote assets loaded when a report is opened are known; the list goes to the job summary. Assert: BAM passes quickcheck and has @RG; steps 20 and 03a exit 0; VCF sample column equals the sample name; step 06 finds the planted ClinVar record with a gene; PharmCAT report.json parses with at least one called gene; pypgx returns a result for CYP2D6; the HTML report has no `.|.` cell. Cache images between runs with a tar cache keyed on versions.env. Steps that need data too large for the runner are listed in docs/testing.md as not covered: VEP offline cache (26 GB), CPSR (bundle plus second cache), AnnotSV annotations (dispatch-only job), GRIDSS (31 GB heap), BWA-MEM2 index build (~90 GB RAM). Triggers: PRs touching scripts/, modules/, workflows/, bin/, conf/, tests/e2e/, tests/fixtures/VERSION, main.nf, nextflow.config or versions.env; monthly cron; dispatch.

Review findings covered: robustness-tests#3, versions#missed, robustness-tests#2, scripts-early#22, robustness-tests#10, security#missed, nextflow#21
acceptance_criteria: The job runs in under 60 minutes, is green on a tree with wave 1 merged, and red when any one assertion is inverted on a scratch branch.

title: Build the HG002 fixture once and store it as a release asset
description:
Nothing in CI runs a tool on real reads (conf/test.config:30-35 is stub-only; container-test runs `--version`). Add scripts/ci/build-fixture.sh: from the public GIAB HG002 60x GRCh38 BAM (`https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.60x.1.bam`, 200 with its .bai) take these regions with mates: chr20:10,000,000-10,500,000 (small variants), chr22:42,000,000-42,300,000 (CYP2D6/CYP2D7 with flanks), chr12:47,800,000-47,950,000 (VDR, pypgx's control gene), chr10:94,700,000-95,000,000 (CYP2C19/CYP2C9), chr6:29,900,000-33,100,000 (HLA), chr5:69,900,000-71,100,000 (SMN1/SMN2), a 300 kb non-PAR chrX slice, a 200 kb PAR1 slice, a 300 kb non-PAR chrY slice (HG002 is male) and chrM, downsampled to ~30x. The chr5, chrX and chrY slices are there from the start so the later paralog, ploidy, sample-QC and Y-haplogroup packages need no fixture rebuild. Emit (a) name-sorted paired FASTQ (`samtools collate | samtools fastq`) so step 02 can run, (b) a mini reference holding whole chr5, chr6, chr10, chr12, chr20, chr22, chrX, chrY and chrM from the pipeline's reference with .fai and .dict, so coordinates stay real, (c) a ClinVar subset for the regions, (d) a ten-record Manta-style SV VCF, (e) a VEP-annotated VCF of at most 200 fixture variants made once in this job with `vep --database --everything` (the offline cache does not fit the runner), so steps 30, 23 and 31 have real CSQ input from wave 1 on, (f) checksums. HG002 is a public, consented GIAB sample, so nothing here is personal data. Upload as release assets from the `build-fixture` job (contents: write on that job only). The release tag is read from `tests/fixtures/VERSION` (first value `fixture-v1`), and the e2e workflow reads the same file, so a later package changes the fixture by editing that one file and the build script, never the workflow. `build-fixture` runs on workflow_dispatch and on a push to a same-repository branch that changes scripts/ci/build-fixture.sh or tests/fixtures/VERSION: a dispatch-only job cannot run before its workflow file is on main, and the e2e job needs the asset on this PR's first run. Document regeneration in docs/testing.md and add the page to mkdocs.yml nav (strict mode fails on an omitted page).

Review findings covered: robustness-tests#3, versions#missed, docs#35, scripts-early#22
acceptance_criteria: The release named in tests/fixtures/VERSION exists with a sha256 file before the e2e job's first run on this PR; the total is under 1.5 GB; `samtools quickcheck` and `gzip -t` pass on download in CI; `samtools idxstats` shows reads on chr5, chr6, chr10, chr12, chr20, chr22, chrX, chrY and chrM.

title: lessons-learned: withdraw the 'pypgx is authoritative for CYP2D6 deletions' lesson and other false lines
description:

It is a launcher, not a labelled wrapper around the old logic, because a wrapper would keep the second scheduler alive and with it the drift this decision is meant to end. The numbered scripts stay as documented single-step commands. A user without Java can still run every step by hand. title: Rewrite renovate.json so it matches the tags this repo uses
description:
renovate.json has existed since April and has never produced a PR (no Renovate PR, no dependency dashboard, no renovate/* branch), and even installed it would propose almost nothing: Docker versioning reads the conda build string after `--` as a compatibility suffix that must match, and that hash changes between versions, so 16 of 31 pins never see a newer tag; `release_116.0` is not a valid Docker version, so VEP gets no updates; the regex `_IMAGE="(?<depName>[^:]+):` half-matches the two digest lines into a package named `...@sha256`, which the 'disabled' rule then does not match; all major updates are disabled; the namespace lists miss several publishers; the two group rules would fold many tools into one PR; no manager covers the Nextflow side. title: run_in wrapper: no network, read-only references, non-root where the image allows
description:
173 of 183 `docker run` lines mount the whole GENOME_DIR read-write, 101 pass `--user root`, none disables networking (scripts/*.sh; e.g. 10-telomere-hunter.sh:28-32 runs a third-party image as root with every sample writable). Outputs are root-owned on Linux, so the printed 'rm -rf to re-run' hints need sudo. Give `run_in` these defaults: `--network none`; `${GENOME_DIR}/reference`, `clinvar` and the cache/bundle directories mounted `:ro`; only `${GENOME_DIR}/${SAMPLE}` read-write; `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp`. Opt-outs are explicit arguments: `--net` for the steps that download (setup, VEP cache install, PGS files, HLA database, Cyrius pip), `--root` for the images settle-doubts row 9 shows cannot run unprivileged (list them in a comment). The engine name comes from `CONTAINER_ENGINE=${CONTAINER_ENGINE:-docker}`. Reword validate-setup.sh:150-151 ('all pipeline Docker images are amd64' is wrong: PharmCAT and VEP ship arm64) to 'most images are amd64'. A side effect worth recording in the PR: with `--network none`, any tool that fetches something at run time (a haplogrep3 tree download, a version check) fails loudly instead of silently reaching out; list what failed and give those steps `--net` with a comment saying what they fetch.

title: scripts/lib/common.sh, sourced by every script; every image comes from versions.env
description:
Argument parsing, the docker call and versions.env sourcing are copied across 51 scripts; 29 scripts hardcode an image and never source versions.env, `staphb/bcftools:1.21` is a literal in 56 places in scripts/ (126 repo-wide), and scripts that do source the file still carry literals (07-pharmacogenomics.sh:27, validate-setup.sh:328) or a silent `2>/dev/null || IMAGE=<copy>` fallback (10-telomere-hunter.sh:27, 18-cnvpytor.sh:25-28) used unquoted. Create scripts/lib/common.sh that resolves the repo root, sources versions.env with no fallback, and exposes `require_image VAR`, `REF_FASTA` (one place for the reference path, today repeated 62 times in 27 scripts; overridable from the environment), `THREADS`, and a `run_in` docker wrapper. Convert every script to source it and to use `${X_IMAGE}` variables, quoted. Move the images that live only in scripts into versions.env: bwa-mem2 (02a:55,68), freebayes (03b:49), strelka (03c:45), tiddit (04a:36), bwa (04b:47 hint), hap.py (benchmark-variants.sh:222). 03-deepvariant.sh must honour DEEPVARIANT_IMAGE. Delete that step in this PR (guard job `image-vars` and control (3) replace it); leave the rest of smoke-test.yml for package ci-one-complete-check. lint.yml's version check keeps passing because it skips every script that sources versions.env.

title: One job that settles the doubts the review could not run
description:
Add scripts/ci/settle-doubts.sh as a dispatch-only job that prints a table to the job summary, one row per question, each with the command and the observed answer: (1) does GATK Mutect2 (step 20) and HaplotypeCaller (03a, INTERVALS=chr20 slice) fail on a BAM made by step 02 with no @RG, and what sample name does DeepVariant write; (2) `telomerehunter --help` in the pinned image: is the default banding hg19; (3) do the two Clair3 model directories hardcoded in scripts/03e-clair3.sh:31,34 exist in the pinned image; (4) what does TIDDIT do when only the BWA-MEM2 index exists (crash, or silent no-assembly); (5) what does `bcftools convert --tsv2vcf -c ID,CHROM,POS,AA` do with a five-column AncestryDNA-style file; (6) AnnotSV exit code without annotations; (7) the first lines VEP prints for `--everything --offline` without `--fasta` (skipped with a note: the cache does not fit the runner); (8) kill the minimap2 container mid-run: is the BAM left behind valid or partial; (9) do the default steps' images run as a non-root uid with a writable /genome mount (list the ones that do not); (10) does T1K's coordinate file built from the reference contain ` -1 -1 ` rows; (11) fastp trimming A/B: DeepVariant on the chr20 slice with and without step 01b, each compared with the GIAB v4.2.1 truth for that slice (hap.py), to decide whether trimming stays the default. title: REVEL: a table whose header matches its columns, and evidence labels at the right strength
description:
docs/00-reference-setup.md:248-264 writes the header of the original nine-column REVEL file over five data columns, so vcfanno's reader takes `ref`/`alt` from the wrong columns and no REVEL value is ever added; steps 23 and 31 then lose that tier without a message. The same block runs bgzip and tabix in staphb/bcftools (which has neither), has no `set -e`, and then deletes the download. Fix: `printf '#chr\tpos\tref\talt\tREVEL\n'` as the header, compress and index in an image that has bgzip and tabix (the GATK image does), start the block with `set -e`. Labels: REVEL 0.644 is PP3 Supporting, 0.773 Moderate, 0.932 Strong, and there is no Very Strong level; correct docs/interpreting-results.md:356-364, docs/00-reference-setup.md:268, docs/30-vcfanno.md:91 and ROADMAP.md:40. Take the BP4 rows from the Pejaver 2022 table itself, not from memory. Label 0.564 as the AlphaMissense class boundary, not an ACMG level. In docs/31-slivar.md say that the step's `REVEL>=0.5` filter is deliberately below the Supporting threshold, or change it; grep the rest of docs/ for other bgzip/tabix calls in the bcftools image and fix them the same way.

description:

title: Input checks: unknown tool names, duplicate samples, missing CNVpytor resources, single-caller merge
description:
main.nf:47 never compares `--tools` entries with the known names, so `--tools vep,clinvar_screen` silently skips ClinVar; duplicate `sample` values share an output directory and the id-keyed joins at main.nf:260-266. workflows/sv.nf:63 calls `file(params.cnvpytor_resources, checkIfExists: true)` with a null default and no db_requirements row, so `--tools cnvpytor` alone dies with a null-file error; the param is missing from nextflow_schema.json. workflows/sv.nf:114-130 lets survivor_merge run with one caller, which emits a header-only consensus. Default tools run PRS and vcfanno without their data (nextflow.config:33): PRS loops over an empty path and vcfanno publishes an unannotated copy of the raw VCF as `<sample>/vep/<sample>_annotated.vcf.gz`. title: SLIVAR module: constraint join that needs no python, and failures that are not swallowed
description:
modules/local/slivar/main.nf:134 gates the gnomAD constraint join on `command -v python3`; the bcftools image has no python, so the else branch (:180-185) always runs and LOEUF/pLI/mis_z never appear, silently. :119-124 ends the compound-het pipe with `|| echo "Compound het detection returned no results"` and the output is `optional: true`, so a slivar crash reads as 'no results'. :142-150 reads `mis_z`/`missense.z_score`, but the gnomAD v4.1 column is `mis.z_score`, and it takes the last transcript row per gene instead of the canonical one. Fix: do the join in awk in the same process (keyed on gene symbol, `canonical == true` rows only, column `mis.z_score`), fail when `--gnomad_constraint` is set and zero genes matched, and let a slivar non-zero exit fail the task. Replace the `A | B || C | D` gnomADe_AF detection at :49-56,:61-68 with the explicit `bcftools +split-vep -l | grep -q gnomADe_AF` test that clinical_filter:51-58 uses.

title: pypgx: report the copy-number call pypgx made, and parse the PharmCAT JSON that 3.2.0 writes
description:
scripts/32-pypgx.sh:201-208 derives 'SV_detected' by substring-matching the diplotype against ['DEL','DUP','x2','x3','*5']: any allele whose name merely contains the '*5' characters is flagged, and the whole-gene deletion names pypgx uses for GSTM1/GSTT1 and CYP2A6 are not in the list, so the null genotypes those genes are included for come out as 'No'. Read the CNV call pypgx stores in results.zip (the CNV column of `pypgx print-data`) and report that value. :262-284 only handles the nested PharmCAT 2.x JSON; on the flat 3.2.0 `genes` map `.get` raises, the broad `except` leaves the comparison empty, every gene is written as 'pypgx only' and the report shows 0 conflicts. Reuse the flat-and-nested logic of scripts/27-cpic-lookup.sh:146-152 and fail loudly when a PharmCAT report was found but zero genes were parsed. Fix docs/32-pypgx.md: :17 says v0.27.0 while the pin is 0.26.0, and :169 says the BAM-based genes fail on 0.26.0 while docs/lessons-learned.md records all genes succeeding; state the image/bundle coupling rule instead.

title: indexcov: read the inferred sex from the right column and compare it with the declared sex
description:
scripts/16-indexcov.sh:46 tests `$6==1`; goleft writes `#family_id sample_id paternal_id maternal_id sex phenotype` with the phenotype column always -9, so the script prints 'female' for every sample. run-all.sh:162 passes `$SEX` as a second argument that the script never reads, and the same unchecked value goes to ExpansionHunter. Fix: read `$5` (1 male, 2 female, anything else unknown), print CNchrX/CNchrY, read the declared sex from `$2` and exit non-zero with a loud message on a mismatch (`SEX_CHECK=warn` downgrades it). Update docs/16-indexcov.md, which presents this step as the sample-identity check.

title: ClinVar screen (bash): normalise and split multiallelics, accept unfiltered callers, check contigs
description:
scripts/06-clinvar-screen.sh:25-42 intersects the un-normalised PASS VCF; isec needs identical REF/ALT, so a multiallelic sample record cannot match a biallelic ClinVar record, and the bash path gives a different answer from modules/local/clinvar_screen/main.nf:38-47, which normalises both sides. `bcftools view -f PASS` (:28) drops every record of a VCF whose FILTER is '.', so pointing the screen at GATK or FreeBayes output yields zero hits with exit 0. `isec -p` writes all four partitions uncompressed (:37-46). Fix: `bcftools norm -m -any -f $REF` on the sample; normalise ClinVar once into `clinvar_pathogenic_chr.norm.vcf.gz` beside the source file (build it here if missing, keyed on mtime) instead of per sample, in bash and in the module; use `-f .,PASS` only when the file has no PASS record at all and print which mode was used; fail when the filtered VCF has zero records; write only the shared records (`isec -n=2 -w1`). Before isec compare contig names of the two files (`bcftools index -s`) and exit with a clear message when none are shared (a ClinVar file with 1,2,.. names against a chr-prefixed reference must not read as zero hits). Keep the literal `clinvar/clinvar_pathogenic_chr.vcf.gz` in the script (it is the source the normalised file is built from): .github/workflows/smoke-test.yml greps step 06 for that exact string until wave 3.

Review findings covered: scripts-early#5, scripts-early#4, scripts-early#29, scripts-late#missed, new-steps#7, nextflow#25, nextflow#29, robustness-tests#10, nextflow#11
acceptance_criteria: e2e: a planted pathogenic allele inside a multiallelic record is reported by bash and by the module; an all-'.' FILTER VCF gives the same hits with a printed notice; a ClinVar file without chr prefixes exits non-zero with the contig message.

title: PRS: no silent fallback to author-build files, no swallowed plink2 errors, honest columns
description:
scripts/25-prs.sh:66-69 falls back from the GRCh38-harmonised file to the author-reported file (often GRCh37 or rsID-only) when the first wget fails, :62 then caches that file for good, and :162 ends plink2 with `2>/dev/null || true` so an old `.sscore` can be reported. :167-168 read `$NF` as the score and `$(NF-1)` as 'variants used', but plink2's default columns end in NAMED_ALLELE_DOSAGE_SUM, SCORE1_AVG, so the 'used' number is a dosage sum and the score is an average over present sites only (modules/local/prs/main.nf:85-98 has the same parsing; scripts/generate-report.sh:236-237 prints the '(N/M variants matched)' text). Fix: remove the fallback and refuse any file whose `#HmPOS_build` header is not GRCh38; download to `.part` then `mv`; `rm -f` the old `.sscore` before scoring; drop the error swallow; add `cols=+scoresums`, read `_SUM`, `ALLELE_CT` by header name and report ALLELE_CT/2 as matched variants. Until the gVCF work lands (package alignment-markdup-gvcf-sex), print one line under every score: 'hom-ref sites are absent from this VCF, so the score is biased; not comparable to published distributions'.

Review findings covered: scripts-late#3, scripts-late#4, nextflow#8, new-steps#3, new-steps#missed, robustness-tests#missed
acceptance_criteria: With the harmonised URL forced to 404 the step exits non-zero and leaves no scoring file; a plink2 failure is reported as a failure; the summary header reads Score_SUM and Variants_Matched and the numbers come from the named columns on the e2e fixture.

title: setup.sh: build the derived ClinVar files whenever they are missing; fix the disk check
description:
scripts/setup.sh:130-165 prints '[OK] ClinVar database already downloaded' when the raw file exists and only builds `clinvar_chr.vcf.gz` and `clinvar_pathogenic_chr.vcf.gz` in the else branch, so a rerun never repairs a missing derived file or index, and validate-setup.sh:215-236 tells the user to run setup.sh, which does nothing. Move both builds out of the else branch and key each on its own `.tbi`. Also: :69 `df -BG` fails on macOS and on a not-yet-created directory, and under pipefail the `|| echo 0` makes the macOS fallback unreachable; use `df -Pk` on the nearest existing parent as validate-setup.sh:134 does. `_download` (:36-47) needs a `curl -fL -C - -o` fallback because stock macOS has no wget while validate-setup.sh:81-82 accepts curl alone. Fix the stale 'step 13's VEP 112' string at validate-setup.sh:255 (step 13 uses 116) and the '~5 GB' PCGR bundle size at setup.sh:259 (7.7 GB upstream).

Review findings covered: robustness-tests#7, scripts-late#21, robustness-tests#24, versions#missed, ci-updates#13

title: CI job: helper binaries each script and module calls exist in the image it runs in

title: Warn when a VCF has no PASS records instead of reporting zero hits

title: One number for steps, loci, runtimes and sizes
description:
Step counts: README 35, pipeline-overview 34, faq 33 (+1), why-local 33+1; run-all runs 34 by default today and fewer once GRIDSS, ancestry and imputation prep are opt-in: state the count in one place only, docs/pipeline-overview.md, and make the other four pages link to it without a number, so adding a step never means editing five pages again. Repeat expansions: pipeline-overview.md:13 and docs/09-str-expansions.md:10,17,53 say '50+ disorders'; the bundled 2021 catalog has 31 loci (index.md:57 is right). Runtimes and sizes disagree between pages: DeepVariant 4-8 h vs 2-4 h, and docs/03-variant-calling.md:27,35 shows 16 CPUs/shards while the script uses 8; BAM 30-40 GB vs 30-80 GB; VEP cache 17 vs 26-30 GB; core downloads 70-75 vs 78 GB; Manta 7,000-9,000 vs 3,000-5,000 SVs; PCGR bundle ~5 GB vs 7.7 GB plus 5.3 GB of AnnotSV annotations. One table in docs/hardware-requirements.md, linked from the other pages. docs/22-survivor-merge.md:7 lists three input callers; the script also merges GRIDSS, Sniffles2 and TIDDIT (and calls TIDDIT '4d'; it is 4a). docs/01b-fastp-qc.md: say `SKIP_TRIM=true` exists and that trimming writes a second FASTQ pair (disk cost). docs/hardware-requirements.md:7,100 says 16 GB RAM is enough while GRIDSS needs a 31 GB heap: say that the default run fits 16 GB and that GRIDSS (opt-in) needs 32 GB or more.

title: versions.yml states the version that ran, and one file collects them
description:
Hardcoded fallback and stub strings disagree with the pins: vcfanno `0.3.7` (pin 0.3.9), annotsv `3.4.4` (3.5.10), mosdepth stub `0.3.13` (0.3.14), gatk stub `4.6.1.0` (4.6.2.0), haplogrep3 `latest` (the pinned digest is 3.2.1); 18 modules carry such literals, and where the probe ends in `| head -1` the `|| echo` fallback can never fire, so a failed probe writes an empty version. versions.yml files are mixed into the MultiQC input (main.nf:278-286), where nothing reads them. Derive each module's version from `task.container` (the tag is the pin), write `unknown` when a live probe fails, and collect all versions.yml into `${outdir}/pipeline_info/software_versions.yml` with `collectFile`.

Review findings covered: nextflow#23, ci-updates#23, versions#27, nextflow#missed
acceptance_criteria: A stub run writes pipeline_info/software_versions.yml whose values equal the tags in versions.env; `grep -rn "echo '[0-9]" modules/` is empty.

CLAUDE.md:182 lists steps '13, 23' to rerun after a VEP cache update; the real chain is 13, 30, 23, 31.

title: Record the deliberate holds and the legacy tools next to their pins
description:
Write the holds where the next maintainer will read them, as comments in versions.env: pypgx stays at 0.26.0 until upstream releases the pandas fix (0.28.0) and the bundle tag matches; plink2 stays at 2.00a5.10 because that is the only versioned tag the publisher ships and it matches pgsc_calc; fastp 1.3.7 waits for a normal suffixed biocontainer tag and Sniffles 2.8.1 for bioconda; Manta, Strelka2, duphold, Cyrius, Octopus and GRIDSS have archived or quiet upstreams and are marked `# legacy: no automated bumps`. The gnomAD constraint table stays on v4.1: the 4.1.2 file is about six times larger and its layout is unread, so no URL swap. Tools already current on 2026-10-01 (minimap2, DeepVariant, AnnotSV, vcfanno, stranger, CNVpytor, duphold, octopus, plink2) need no action.

Review findings covered: versions#23, versions#24, versions#22, versions#19, versions#25, versions#30, ci-updates#missed
acceptance_criteria: Each hold has a one-line comment with its reason and exit condition in versions.env.

title: Scatter the single-process callers per chromosome
description:
scripts/03a-gatk-haplotypecaller.sh:43-61 and 03b-freebayes.sh run the whole genome in one process (only PairHMM is threaded), and scripts/29-mutect2-somatic.sh does the same when a whole-genome run is requested. title: KIR typing as a second T1K pass
description:
